title: ACE2-NEMO: Coupling an ML atmospheric emulator to a full-depth dynamical ocean model
abstract: Understanding how fast atmospheric variability shapes slow climate variability and sensitivity remains a central challenge in Earth-system science. Recent advances in machine-learned (ML) atmospheric models have demonstrated remarkable skill on weather timescales, but their emergent behaviour in a fully coupled climate system remains largely unexplored. We present early results from a new hybrid modelling framework, in which the ACE2 ML atmospheric emulator is interactively coupled to the NEMO ocean model. We report on a set of 70-year coupled simulations (1950-2020 historical forcing and fixed-1950s control). These experiments represent, to our knowledge, the first multi-decadal integrations of a machine-learned atmosphere interacting with a full-depth dynamical ocean. Several historical and fixed-1950s control simulations from the fully dynamic global coupled climate model EC-Earth, which has the same ocean component used in ACE2-NEMO, are also considered for comparison. We assess the behaviour of the coupled system, with particular focus on low-frequency tropical variability and the climate response to greenhouse-gas forcing. Analysis of potentially emergent El Niño-like variability reveals realistic fast timescale air-sea coupling in the tropical Pacific, but the temporal variability is unrealistic, with very low amplitude oscillations; this appears to be due to weak atmospheric feedback in the tropical Pacific. The response to CO2 forcing shows initial agreement with EC-Earth3P, but deviates due to reduced downward short-wave radiation in ACE2. These results provide a unique test of physical realism for atmospheric emulators, and evaluate the possible role of entirely machine-learned components in next-generation Earth system models.
problem: While machine-learned atmospheric models show skill on weather timescales, their emergent behavior and physical realism when coupled with a full-depth dynamical ocean for multi-decadal climate simulations remain largely unexplored, presenting a significant test for their use in next-generation Earth system models.
method: A hybrid modeling framework is proposed that interactively couples a machine-learned atmospheric emulator (ACE2) with a dynamical ocean model (NEMO) via a shared-storage infrastructure, enabling multi-decadal climate simulations to test the emergent behavior and physical realism of the atmospheric emulator.
task: The task is to couple a machine-learned atmospheric emulator (ACE2) with a full-depth dynamical ocean model (NEMO) and assess the resulting hybrid system's behavior, stability, and physical realism in multi-decadal climate simulations.
innovation: This paper presents the first multi-decadal simulations from ACE2-NEMO, a novel hybrid model that interactively couples a machine-learned atmospheric emulator with a full-depth dynamical ocean model to test the emulator's physical realism and emergent behavior in a fully coupled climate system.

To investigate the model's ability to simulate coupled variability, we explore how well ACE2-NEMO represents El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Our analysis reveals that, whilst ACE2-NEMO produces realistic spatial correlations of precipitation, sea level pressure and winds, the Niño 3.4 index time series of ACE2-NEMO is extremely muted compared to observations, and lacks realistic temporal variability.

kg_extraction_triplets.target_entity_instance: simple bulk formulae for heat fluxes over ice
kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: Through developing the coupling, several problems were identified relating to the ACE2 fluxes over sea ice; the sensible heat fluxes produced by ACE2 over sea ice did not seem to be consistent with the temperature differences, and there were large drifts in sea ice volume and sea surface temperature. These problems were solved by using simple bulk formulae to calculate heat fluxes over ice.
